answer: An agent economy can make each new identity earn trust through a slowly released stake: agents lock tokens, then receive small task batches whose results are checked against independent reviewers. A mismatched result forfeits part of the stake and delays access to larger jobs. Copying one agent into a hundred identities no longer creates free influence; the attacker must fund and maintain a separate stake for each, while risking losses. A relic-market task on the terrace or wharf is still judged by the same checks.
